title: Corrections Log
kicker: Every factual correction on proudtek.com — the original text, the fix, and the date
summary: This is the single public record of every factual correction issued on proudtek.com. When an article stated something factually wrong — a wrong number, standard identifier, chip family, or regulatory date — the original text, the corrected text, and the date are logged here. Our readers are procurement teams who cross-check specs against vendor datasheets, so we treat errors in specs, certifications, and standards references as high-priority and fix them in the open. Typos and clarity edits that change no factual claim are made silently under our editorial policy and are not listed here.
heroPoints: We never edit a factual claim away silently. The original wording stays visible beside the correction.
Anyone can request a correction — readers, reviewers, or the editorial board — at editors@proudtek.com.
We acknowledge within 2 business days and resolve a verified correction within 5, or reply in writing explaining why the original stands.
A retracted article is never deleted. It is replaced with a notice explaining the retraction and a link to what supersedes it.
imageAlt: The life of a Proud Tek correction: a reader flags a claim, we review it against a primary source, we correct it or explain why not, a 90-day banner goes on the article, and the entry is logged here permanently.

sections.title: What each label means
sections.intro: A change reaches this log only when it fixes a factual claim. We use four labels, and we call each one by its name — a correction is never softened into a "recast" or a "tweak."

features.title: Correction
features.text: A substantive factual error: a wrong spec, memory size, read range, standard identifier, chip name, or date. The article is fixed and the original claim is quoted in the log — e.g. "It is NXP NTAG 213, not NTAG 216."

features.title: Clarification
features.text: The facts were right, but the wording was ambiguous or incomplete enough to mislead. We sharpen the language and note what changed; no underlying claim was wrong.

features.title: Editor's note
features.text: An error serious enough to change how the whole article should be read, or a standards or disclosure issue. It is added to the top of the piece with a plain explanation.

features.title: Retraction
features.text: The core claim could not be defended against its source. The original is not deleted — it is replaced with a notice and a link to the content that supersedes it.

callout.label: No euphemisms
callout.text: When we get a fact wrong we call it a correction — not a "fix," a "recast," or an "update." The rule that decides whether a change is made silently or logged here lives in our [editorial policy](/about/editorial-policy/).

sections.title: Where a correction appears
sections.intro: How prominently a correction shows up scales with how serious the error was.
bullets: Serious errors: a correction banner is placed at the top of the article, above the first paragraph.
Minor factual fixes: a dated note is appended at the foot of the article and flagged inline where the claim sits.
The banner stays on the article for 90 days after the correction date, then comes down — but the entry remains in this log indefinitely.
Retracted articles keep their notice permanently; the page itself may become a redirect to the superseding content after 12 months.

sections.title: How to request a correction
sections.intro: The process is deliberately simple, because a correction culture only works if the readers who spot an error actually send it in. Email editors@proudtek.com — one address, monitored by the editorial board.
checklist: The article URL and the specific claim you believe is wrong.
What you think the correct statement should be.
A primary source that supports it — a standards document, OEM datasheet, or regulator page. (What qualifies is defined in our [sourcing standards](/about/editorial-policy/).)
Whether you would like to be credited by name; we log "external reader" unless you opt in.

items.label: Within 2 business days — Acknowledged
items.text: You get a reply confirming the request has arrived and who is reviewing it.

items.label: Within 5 business days — Resolved
items.text: We publish the correction, or reply in writing explaining why the original text stands. A case that needs a lab re-test is given an ETA instead.

items.label: Logged — Permanent
items.text: A published correction is added to the log below with the original text, the change, and the date. It is never removed.

callout.label: We reply either way
callout.text: Even when we decline to change an article — because the cited source is not authoritative, or the original was already right — we reply with the reasoning. Declining in silence would defeat the purpose.

sections.title: Correction log
sections.intro: The record below is authoritative and ordered newest first. It logs factual corrections and clarifications only — typos, broken links, and wording tidies that change no claim are made silently. When no correction has been issued, the placeholder row stays put as an honest indicator rather than being hidden.

rows: No factual corrections have been issued since this log opened on 2026-04-17.

callout.label: What a future entry looks like
callout.text: A row will read: date · article · the original claim, quoted · the corrected claim, quoted · submitter / primary source. For example, an article that referred to "the ISO 14443 standard" corrected to cite "ISO/IEC 14443-3:2018." The table updates in place the moment the first correction lands.

faq.question: Why keep the original wrong text in the log?
faq.answer: Because a fix made silently is indistinguishable from an error that never happened. An editorial record with no visible errors has either never been challenged or is hiding them. Keeping the original text beside the correction is what makes the fix — and our sources — verifiable by anyone who read the earlier version.

faq.question: Do you ever remove an entry from the log?
faq.answer: No. A correction entry is permanent. The only exception is when a correction itself turns out to be wrong: we add a new row that supersedes the earlier one, but neither row is deleted.

faq.question: Can I request a correction anonymously?
faq.answer: Yes. Email editors@proudtek.com and say you would like to stay anonymous. The entry will credit "external reader" and we will not share your identity.
